company_description: Analog Devices, Inc. engages in the design, manufacture, testing, and marketing of integrated circuits (ICs), software, and subsystems products in the United States, rest of North and South America, Europe, Japan, China, and rest of Asia. It provides data converter products, which translate real-world analog signals into digital data, as well as translates digital data into analog signals; power management and reference products for power conversion, driver monitoring, sequencing, and energy management applications in the automotive, communications, industrial, and consumer markets; and power ICs that include performance, integration, and software design simulation tools for accurate power supply designs. The company also offers amplifiers to condition analog signals; and radio frequency and microwave ICs to support cellular infrastructure; and micro-electro-mechanical systems technology solutions, including accelerometers used to sense acceleration, gyroscopes for sense rotation, inertial measurement units to sense multiple degrees of freedom, and broadband switches for radio and instrument systems, as well as isolators. kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned from the sale of products and services during the year.
kpis.description: Revenue increased by 17% in 2025, driven by broad-based demand and customer inventory normalization.
kpis.signal: Strong double-digit growth despite a high base.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved by 440 basis points to 61.5%, supported by better manufacturing capacity utilization and lower amortization of intangibles.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement due to better factory utilization.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit relative to revenue, after all operating expenses.
kpis.description: Calculated as (Revenue - COGS - R&D - SMGA - Amortization - Special charges) / Revenue, it increased from 23.84% to 26.63%.
kpis.signal: Strong improvement in operating margin, indicating operational efficiency.

kpis.name: R&D Investment as % of Revenue
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue invested in research and development.
kpis.description: R&D expenses reached $1,766 million in 2025, or 16% of revenue, in line with the prior year (15.8%).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all expenses, taxes, and interest.
kpis.description: Net income surged by 39%, rising from $1,635 million to $2,267 million, supported by margin expansion and revenue growth.
kpis.signal: Faster net income growth than revenue, reflecting operating leverage.

kpis.name: Diluted Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Earnings per share, accounting for all potentially dilutive securities.
kpis.description: Diluted EPS increased from $3.28 to $4.56, reflecting a significant improvement in per-share profitability.
kpis.signal: Strong EPS growth, indicating enhanced value creation per share.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of people employed by the company.
kpis.description: The company employs approximately 13,000 engineers, highlighting its technical orientation and commitment to continuous innovation, enabling strong customer positioning.
kpis.signal: Approximately 13,000 engineers, a key advantage for innovation and technological differentiation.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €47.99 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.description: Annual consolidated revenue, values extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last seven fiscal years from 10-K filings.
kpis.signal: Revenue of $11.02 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: AI Data Center Revenue Growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in revenue from data center infrastructure for artificial intelligence applications.
kpis.description: The Communications segment grew 26% ($1,377,865 thousand in 2025 vs $1,091,431 in 2024), driven by growth in wireline solutions for AI-enabled data center infrastructure.
kpis.signal: Key trend fueled by global expansion of AI data centers, Communications segment +26%.

kpis.name: Industrial Segment Growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in revenue in the industrial market, primarily test equipment and defense.
kpis.description: The industrial segment grew 15% ($4,929,409 thousand in 2025 vs $4,290,324 in 2024), aided by customer inventory normalization, test equipment, and aerospace and defense applications.
kpis.signal: Recovery in industrial orders following inventory normalization, growth in test and aerospace/defense.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share

kpis.description: Five-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance ex-div dates.

kpis.explanation: Annual total: dividends paid + share buybacks.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends and buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source: yfinance cashflow.

kpis.explanation: Portion of net income distributed. >80% = potentially unsustainable.

kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate profit per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).

risks.title: Global Geopolitical and Trade Instability
risks.summary: ADI operates globally (Ireland, Philippines, Thailand, Malaysia) and relies heavily on international customers. Geopolitical tensions (Taiwan, Russia-Ukraine, Middle East), U.S.-China trade restrictions, and 2025 tariffs directly threaten its operations and revenues.
risks.score_rationale: Risk ranked first in the report with highly intense language ('could materially and adversely affect'). Increasing trend: Taiwan tensions, China export restrictions, and 2025 tariffs explicitly mentioned as new. Geopolitical category = high weight for semiconductor sector.

risks.title: Export Restrictions and Technology Controls
risks.summary: U.S. export restrictions limit sales to certain Chinese companies. These restrictions have expanded over years, impacting revenues and pushing customers to seek alternative suppliers or develop their own capacity.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk in a dedicated section with critical language ('could be materially harmed', 'continue to expand'). Increasing trend: restrictions 'have continued to expand for several years'. Direct impact on China revenue documented. Regulation = high weight.

risks.title: Critical Dependence on Third-Party Foundries (TSMC)
risks.summary: ADI relies on external foundries for over 50% of its wafers, particularly TSMC. Geopolitical tensions in Taiwan or capacity constraints could halt production and paralyze operations.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk with intense language ('could adversely affect our business and results of operations'). Stable but structural trend: over 50% of wafers from third parties. Taiwan tensions explicitly linked to TSMC. Industrial = high weight.

risks.title: Market Cyclicality and Overcapacity Risk
risks.summary: The semiconductor sector is cyclical: overproduction leads to overcapacity and price declines, while undercapacity limits demand fulfillment. 2025 tariffs and trade uncertainties amplify this volatility.
risks.score_rationale: Risk placed mid-report with moderate language ('may be adversely affected', 'could materially and adversely affect'). Stable trend: cyclicality inherent to the sector. New context: tariffs and trade restrictions amplify volatility.

risks.title: Dependence on Independent Distributors
risks.summary: 56% of revenue comes from independent distributors without credit guarantees. ADI has no protection against payment default or bankruptcy. Termination or consolidation in distribution could severely disrupt operations.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk: 56% of revenue via third-party distributors. Moderate language but clear financial impact ('could adversely affect our operating results'). Stable trend but worsened by tariffs/export controls. Credit = high weight (no letters of credit).

risks.title: Manufacturing Operations Disruptions
risks.summary: ADI operates factories in the USA, Ireland, Philippines, Thailand, and Malaysia. Any prolonged disruption (cyberattack, natural disaster, epidemic) could halt production and cause customer loss.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk with intense language ('could materially and adversely affect'). Stable trend but aggravated context: cyberattacks, natural disasters, pandemics explicitly mentioned. Facilities in high-risk zones (Philippines, Thailand, Malaysia).

risks.title: 2025 Tariffs and Trade Restrictions
risks.summary: In 2025, the U.S. government announced broad and targeted tariffs, followed by countermeasures. An investigation into imported semiconductors (April 2025) could impose new tariffs. This increases raw material costs and creates economic uncertainty.
risks.score_rationale: New risk explicitly dated (2025). Highly intense language ('materially and adversely affect'). Increasing trend: ongoing investigations (semiconductors April 2025), tariffs announced then partially lifted, creating volatility. Regulation = high weight.

risks.title: Product Diversion to Gray Market
risks.summary: Some ADI products are diverted to the gray market and resold without authorization. This creates regulatory compliance and reputational risks if products are used for unauthorized purposes.
risks.score_rationale: Risk placed at the end of the report with moderate language ('could result in reputational harm'). Stable trend: historical issue ('in the past, certain of our products have been'). Reputational and compliance impact, but less critical than geopolitical/supply chain.
